subject: Atlas Retail — Pilot dedicated capacity: initial questionnaire and sample traffic
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@atlasretail.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-11T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot sizing — quick start and traffic snapshot

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking this — we’re lining up a 3-week pilot (search + recommendations + chat assist) to replace a portion of our inference stack. The pilot target window is late August; we need a rough dedicated sizing estimate to lock budget and confirm SLA targets.

Quick context: Atlas Retail runs user-facing search and a contextual chat assistant. Expected peak user concurrency is unclear; problems we want to avoid are tail latencies > 300ms p99 for search and > 600ms p99 for chat. We prefer a conservative starting commitment and then rightsize after telemetry.

Attached is a small telemetry snapshot from last 7 days (token counts are obfuscated). It includes a distribution of prompt and response lengths and an hourly breakdown.

Could you send your pre-sales questionnaire for dedicated sizing and let us know any examples you need (sample prompts, request/response mixes, percent streaming vs full-response)?

Appreciate it — Emily

[attachment: atlas_traffic_snapshot.csv (CSV, 78KB)]

Emily Chen
Head of Applied ML
Atlas Retail
emily.chen@atlasretail.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing — quick start and traffic snapshot

Hi Emily — thanks for the snapshot and context. Short answer: we can get you a conservative dedicated sizing estimate with the data you already shared, and a tighter plan once we get sample prompt artifacts.

Attached is our preflight questionnaire (PDF) that covers traffic shape, concurrency, session behavior, prompt/response length distributions, streaming vs non-streaming split, and allowed fallbacks. The checklist also includes a short section for expected SLA targets and any regulatory constraints.

A few clarifying asks to speed the sizing:
- Can you confirm what percent of requests are stateful (session-bound KV cache needed) vs stateless?
- Do you expect long-running streaming responses for the chat (partial tokens sent periodically) or mostly full-response returns?
- For search, are you running re-ranking on top-N or full generation for each query?
- Any hard requirements on inference region (we can run US-west / US-east or cross-region fallback)?

If you can send a small sample of 200–500 anonymized prompt/response pairs (or the attached XLSX format), Ben and Karthik will run an initial tokenization and latency model and return a sizing ballpark.

I’ll schedule a 30min sizing sync for early next week — propose Tue 7/17 10:00am PT. Let me know if that works.

Cheers,

Tessa Morgan
Solutions Lead, Pre-Sales
Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_preflight_questionnaire.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@atlasretail.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-11T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing — quick start and traffic snapshot

Emily — quick technical note from the sizing side. Appreciate the snapshot file. To produce a realistic GPU fleet plan we need:

1) Prompt length distribution broken into buckets (0-32, 33-128, 129-512, 513-2048 tokens) and average response length for each bucket.
2) Session stickiness: fraction of traffic that reuses KV cache within a 10-minute window. Even coarse buckets (0-10%, 10-50%, 50-90%) are useful.
3) Expected QPS and target p95/p99 latency targets per route (search vs chat vs rerank).
4) Percent of requests requiring large context (>=4096 tokens).

I attached a template XLSX — put your sample prompt/response pairs into the sheet, and include a short column describing whether streaming is used for each chat example. With that I’ll run a quick estimator that generates expected GPU-hours and suggested oversubscription factors.

If you don’t have time to fill the sheet, a 10–15 sample set is enough to get a first pass; we can bootstrap the rest from the CSV you sent.

Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[attachment: sample_prompts_and_lengths.xlsx (XLSX, 56KB)]

From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@atlasretail.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-12T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing — quick start and traffic snapshot

Thanks Tessa & Ben — attached are 250 anonymized prompt/response rows exported to the template (sheet: "sample_prompts"). High-level answers inline below for quick reference: 

- Stateful fraction: ~35% of chat requests reuse session context within 10 minutes. Search is stateless.
- Streaming: ~20% of chat responses use streaming (long summaries). Most are full-response returns.
- Search flow: user query -> top-100 re-rank -> generate snippet for top 3. Re-ranking is on-device for some customers but we will route 30% of re-ranks to Redwood full-generation for the pilot.
- Prompt distribution (approx): 0-32: 18%; 33-128: 47%; 129-512: 28%; 513-2048+: 7%. Average response lengths: 24, 86, 340, 960 tokens respectively.
- Peak QPS estimate (per recent campaign): 550 QPS aggregated across endpoints; expected pilot peak ~150 QPS once routing is staged. Target p99: search <= 300ms, chat <= 600ms.

Attached files: atlas_traffic_snapshot.csv (you already have), and sample_prompts_and_lengths.xlsx (sheet: sample_prompts).

Happy to hop on Tue 7/17 10:00am PT — confirmed on my side.

Best,
Emily
Head of Applied ML
Atlas Retail
[attachment: sample_prompts_and_lengths.xlsx (XLSX, 36KB)]
